meeting_header:
Date: 2025-01-28 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Laura Martinez (Acme - Head of ML), Samir Patel (Acme - Platform Eng), Maya Johnson (Acme - PM)
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for Acme's multi-lingual customer support assistant. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments; context length needs (16k vs 32k vs 100k), multilingual coverage, and tool-calling/function support. Agreed to run benchmarks on Hosted with 16k/32k context models and to share security docs and pricing.
topics: model selection: open model comparisons (Llama2, Mistral, MPT, Red team variants)
context length requirements (16k, 32k, 100k) and cost implications
deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're here to talk through model selection and how Redwood can fit into Acme's stack. Um, quick intros?
[00:12] Laura: Hi I'm Laura, head of ML at Acme. We're building a customer support assistant, need multi-language support (EN/ES/FR/JA) and long context for conversation history.
[00:23] Samir: Samir here, platform eng, mostly concerned about data residency, VPC, and latency to our EU cluster.
[00:30] Maya: Maya, product, focused on UX and tool integrations, like calendar and order lookup.
[00:37] Alex: Great, Priya is our SE who will run through the technicals. Priya?
[00:42] Priya: thanks alex. So high level questions: what sort of context lengths are you expecting per convo, and are you doing retrieval + tool calling?
[00:50] Laura: We want 20-30k tokens of context typically for long threads, sometimes up to ~50k for a full conversation thread. We'll do retrieval for KB + invoices and need tool calls into order API.
[01:05] Priya: ok that pushes towards models with 32k or 100k support. For open models we usually compare Llama 2 variants, Mistral, MPT, and some of the newer high-context models — the tradeoffs are cost, latency, and hallucination rate.
[01:20] Samir: quick question — hosted vs dedicated vs private. We have some PII in logs and certain EU customers require data residency. What's the path there?
[01:29] Alex: good q. Hosted gives fastest time to value; data is encrypted and we offer retention controls, but for strict residency or dedicated tenancy we recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with predictable throughput and better isolation. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for compliance — you manage networking and keys.
[01:45] Laura: how different is performance and latency between hosted and dedicated?
[01:50] Priya: Dedicated latency is usually lower and more predictable since you have reserved pools, less noisy neighbors. Hosted can be almost as fast on common models but has more variance under heavy load. Cost per token tends to be lower on Dedicated for sustained throughput.
[02:05] Maya: and function-calling - does Redwood support tool-calls like OpenAI function call?
[02:10] Priya: yes we support function/tool-calling and structured output. There are also considerations: some open models have better formatted responses out-of-the-box, others need instruction tuning or small instruction-following adapters.
[02:22] Laura: multilingual — we've seen inconsistent Spanish and Japanese handling in some models. Which open models do you recommend?
[02:29] Priya: short list: Llama 2 13B/70B (good baseline but multilingual varies), Mistral-Instruct flavors have strong English and decent EU languages, MPT-32k variants are optimized for long context, and a couple of community models with 100k context (they're experimental). We often recommend testing 13B chat and 70B or mixes — or opt for quantized 4-bit to balance cost.
[02:50] Alex: also mention Redwood-verified performance profiles — we run micro-benchmarks so we can share a matrix of latencies/throughput for these models on common hardware.
[02:59] Samir: when you say 100k context, what's the real impact on cost and latency?
[03:05] Priya: it's significant. Memory and compute increase linearly-ish with sequence length. Batching becomes harder; KV cache management helps for repeated prefixes. For 100k you likely need different kernels and potentially model parallelism which increases resource cost.
[03:20] Laura: are there tokenization issues for Japanese? We've seen tokenizers blow up token counts.
[03:26] Priya: yes, tokenization varies — some tokenizers split Japanese into many tokens. We recommend running a sample tokenization pass during the benchmark and include both normalization and detokenization checks.
[03:37] Maya: on tool calling, we need secure calls to our order API and redaction for PII. Can Redwood help with middleware?
[03:45] Alex: yes we provide function-calling primitives and you can route tool calls through your VPC or via our secure outbound connectors. Also audit logs capture calls; we can show examples.
[03:55] Samir: about KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[03:58] Priya: yes, for Dedicated and Private you can plug in your KMS/HSM. Hosted supports envelope encryption and customer key options in enterprise tiers.
[04:08] Alex: any concerns on hallucinations for order lookups?
[04:12] Laura: we need deterministic behavior when calling order lookup — hallucination risk is high. Retrieval + deterministic function calling is the plan.
[04:20] Priya: exactly — recommended pattern is RAG + strict function output parsing + confidence scoring. We can enforce fallback behaviors.
[04:28] Maya: ok we also need multi-turn context retention with persona and system instructions — can Redwood pin system prompts?
[04:35] Priya: yes you can pin prompts, manage per-route defaults, and do canary rollouts for prompt changes.
[04:42] Alex: let's talk about latency SLOs — what are you targeting?
[04:46] Samir: 300-500ms p95 for chat-like responses, up to 2s acceptable for longer generation for heavy contexts.
[04:54] Priya: p95 in 300-500ms is feasible on smaller models (13B) with dedicated infra; 70B or bigger will be higher unless actively optimized (quantization + faster kernels). We'll share benchmarks.
[05:06] Laura: do you support quantized models (4-bit) and do you notice quality regressions?
[05:11] Priya: yes we support INT4/FP4 quantization paths; quality can be close to FP16 for many instruction-following tasks, but we recommend sanity tests and downstream evals. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload.
[05:26] Alex: curious — what's your current stack?
[05:28] Laura: we use a mix: embeddings with vendor X, in-house retriever, and Athena DB for logs. Currently using OpenAI for a few agents but cost is high.
[05:36] Alex: ok sounds typical. For comparison, we'll propose a matrix: candidate models, expected latency, cost per 1M tokens, multilingual score, and tool-calling compatibility.
[05:47] Maya: will you include inference cost estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[05:50] Alex: yes, we'll show both. Dedicated has committed cost advantages for sustained throughput.
[05:57] Samir: about benchmarking: can we run tests against our EU region?
[06:01] Priya: yes for Dedicated/Private we can deploy in region; Hosted has regions too. For the initial benchmarking we'll run against Hosted EU endpoints to measure network lat.
[06:12] Laura: question on model updates — how do rollouts work? we need ability to pin older model versions per route.
[06:17] Priya: you can pin model versions and have canary/A-B rollouts with automatic fallback to previous stable variant.
[06:24] Maya: what about security docs? we need SOC2, penetration test summary, and audit logs examples.
[06:29] Alex: we'll share SOC2 and a redacted pentest summary, plus docs on audit logs and retention.
[06:36] Samir: curious about KV cache — you mentioned prefix caching earlier. How does that work with long context?
[06:42] Priya: KV cache stores key/value activations so when you have repeated prefixes it avoids recomputing. For long context, we do chunked KV and smart eviction, but large contexts still hit memory.
[06:53] Laura: any advice around fine-tuning vs adapters/LoRA? We want custom behavior for our domain language.
[06:59] Priya: LoRA/adapters are usually faster and cheaper to iterate; full fine-tune gives best control but costs more and is heavier operationally. Also consider instruction tuning or retrieval to minimize fine-tuning needs.
[07:12] Alex: let's do a quick rough recommendation — for multi-lingual + 30k typical context, start with a 13B-32k optimized model in hosted for an initial pilot, then scale to Dedicated if throughput grows. For edge cases needing 100k, evaluate specialized high-context models and Private deployment if you need residency.
[07:29] Samir: that sounds pragmatic. How long to spin up a Dedicated environment?
[07:33] Alex: provisioning depends on capacity and region — typically 2-8 weeks for reserved pools; Private can be longer for on-prem. Hosted is immediate.
[07:43] Maya: on cost — can you give a ballpark per 1M tokens for 13B hosted vs dedicated?
[07:49] Alex: ballpark only: Hosted 13B might be X$/1M tokens, Dedicated lower per token at high volumes — we'll put numbers in the matrix.
[07:58] Laura: sample prompts — we'll share a set of prompts in Spanish and Japanese for benchmarking.
[08:03] Priya: great, include short and long prompts and expected extraction fields for tool responses.
[08:10] Samir: for the benchmarking harness, can we push our own Docker to Redwood for private workloads?
[08:15] Priya: for Private deployments yes; for Hosted we provide runbooks and a test harness. For Dedicated we can run customer-provided containers in some cases — we'll follow up.
[08:27] Alex: any blockers that would prevent a pilot?
[08:30] Laura: need legal review for data flow and a basic security questionnaire answered.
[08:34] Alex: we'll send the security questionnaire and SOC2 docs.
[08:37] Maya: timeline — aiming to start pilot in 3-4 weeks.
[08:41] Alex: reasonable. We'll target to get the benchmark scheduled within 1 week and have pricing in 2-3 business days.
[08:49] Priya: ok last technical note — function-calling edge cases: some models may hallucinate field names; enforce schema validation on the caller side. Also we support streaming responses with incremental function invocation.
[09:03] Samir: streaming is important for low perceived latency.
[09:07] Priya: yep we have streaming tokens + partial function outputs.
[09:12] Laura: any recommended eval metrics for multilingual? BLEU/CHRF are ok but we prefer task-specific metrics and human eval.
[09:19] Priya: agree, automated metrics plus small human sample is best. We'll help set up eval harness.
[09:26] Alex: quick recap and next steps?
[09:29] Laura: yes please.
[09:30] Alex: we'll send model matrix, pricing, SOC2/KMS docs, and propose benchmark slots. Priya will lead technical deep dive and benchmarking.
[09:41] Priya: I'll follow up with a proposed test plan and tokenized sample counts.
[09:46] Samir: I'll send a dataset extract and PII redaction rules.
[09:50] Maya: schedule the kickoff once we have security signoff.
[09:54] Alex: perfect. Thanks everyone.
[09:57] Laura: thanks all.
